bitfield.description: Fractional Radio Timer.

bitenum.token: Disable fractional compensation, i.e. use normal timer. Normal RAT tick frequency is the RF Core input clock frequency down-divided by 12 (i.e. typically 48 MHz / 12 = 4 MHz -- giving a RAT tick period of 250 ns).
bitenum.description: Disable fractional compensation, i.e. use normal timer. Normal RAT tick frequency is the RF Core input clock frequency down-divided by 12 (i.e. typically 48 MHz / 12 = 4 MHz -- giving a RAT tick period of 250 ns).

bitenum.token: Enable compensated timer. If the RF Core input clock frequency has a small offset from the expected 48 MHz, the normal divide-by-12 can be replaced with a fractional down-divider to compensate for the skewed input clock and still achieve the normal 4 MHz RAT tick period. With fractional compensation, the RF Core input clock is down-divided by a fractional value (12 + ε), where ε is a small adjustment value configured in the RATCOMP register.
bitenum.description: Enable compensated timer. With fractional compensation, the RF Core input clock is down-divided by a fractional value (12 + ε), where ε is a small adjustment value configured in the RATCOMP register.

Controls fractional compensation of the RAT tick frequency. When fractional compensation is enabled in RATCFG.FRACRAT, the RF Core input clock is divided down by value 12*(1 + RATCOMP/2^21), where RATCOMP is a 16-bit signed value, to still generate the normal tick frequency of 4.0 MHz. This means the fractionally compensated clock divider has a configurable value in range [11.813, 12.187], which means it can compensate for an RF Core input clock frequency in the range [47.250, 48.750] MHz.
